_about: Gadget Studio additions to the vendored sim assumptions (sim-assumptions.json). Same convention: 'basis' says where each number comes from. ASSUMPTION = no source yet; replace with supplier quotes, courier API results or measured times.

padding_mm_per_side.basis: ASSUMPTION: outer box = assembly bounding box + 40 mm padding per side (the sim used a fixed 22 x 18 x 20 cm box for a 108 x 78 x 124 mm robot)

box_and_padding_kg.basis: ASSUMPTION: corrugated box, insert, manual card

electronics_kg.basis: ASSUMPTION: core board, backplane, modules, cables, fasteners (library has no masses yet)

assembly_ops_rule.basis: ASSUMPTION: same operation set as the sim (sim-assumptions.json assembly.minutes_per_op); counts come from this design: one module_install per mounted module, one cable_route per 3 harness cables (minimum 1), one insert_heatset per heat-set insert in the hardware list

parts_procurement_days.basis: ASSUMPTION: Indian distributor stock (Robu / Robocraze class), metro delivery; not checked against live stock

pcb_fabrication_days.basis: ASSUMPTION: 2-layer prototype backplane from a PCB fab including shipping; zero once populated backplanes are stocked

print_hours_per_day.basis: ASSUMPTION: one FDM printer, overnight runs, plate changes during the day

assembly_flash_test_days.basis: ASSUMPTION: assembly, flashing and the functional test on one working day; first article may take two

remake_buffer_days.basis: ASSUMPTION: one failed print or QC rework

courier_days.basis: ASSUMPTION: Indian courier metro to non-metro; a real window needs the delivery pincode and a courier serviceability API (blueprint §8.5)
